__Goal:__ Prevent abuse, manage costs associated with LLM API calls, and ensure fair usage, especially during pilots\.

__Why it's needed:__ LLM calls \(especially to powerful models like GPT\-4 or Gemini Pro\) can get expensive quickly\. A single user, intentionally or unintentionally \(e\.g\., a script, a stuck loop, or just very enthusiastic testing\), could generate significant costs\.

__Implementation Strategy: Backend\-Centric with Frontend Awareness__

__	•	A\. Backend Implementation \(Primary Enforcement\):__

__	•	Mechanism:__

__	•	Request Counting:__ Track the number of "significant AI requests" per user \(or per project, or per user within a project\) over a defined period \(e\.g\., daily, weekly, monthly for pilots\)\. "Significant AI requests" are those that trigger expensive LLM calls \(e\.g\., summarization, "Ask Project Docs" Q&A, title/bullet/outline generation\)\. Purely local UI interactions or metadata fetches might not count\.

__	•	Token Counting \(More Precise but More Complex\):__ For even finer\-grained control, track the total number of input \+ output tokens processed by the LLM for each user\. This directly correlates with cost\.

__	•	Where to Track:__

	•	In your __Relational Database \(Users table or a dedicated UserUsageStats table\):__

	•	userID \(FK\)

	•	period\_start\_date \(e\.g\., daily reset\)

	•	request\_count\_today

	•	token\_count\_today \(if implementing token tracking\)

	•	last\_request\_timestamp

__	•	Enforcement Logic \(in API Gateway or a dedicated RateLimitingService before Core Services\):__

	•	Before processing a significant AI request, check the user's current usage against their limit\.

	•	If the limit is exceeded, return a specific HTTP error code \(e\.g\., 429 Too Many Requests\) with a user\-friendly message\.

__	•	Limit Configuration:__

	•	Store limits \(e\.g\., daily\_request\_limit\_mvp, daily\_token\_limit\_mvp\) in your config\.py or a database configuration table\. Make them easily adjustable\.

	•	For MVP/pilots, start with a "generous but not infinite" daily limit\.

__	•	Resetting Limits:__ A scheduled job \(e\.g\., a cron job or serverless function\) can reset the daily/weekly counts at the appropriate interval\.

__	•	B\. Frontend Awareness & User Feedback:__

__	•	Displaying Usage \(Optional for MVP, but good for transparency\):__

	•	The Web App could subtly display "X / Y requests used today" in the user profile section or a settings page\.

__	•	Handling 429 Too Many Requests Error:__

	•	Both the Web App and PowerPoint Add\-in MUST gracefully handle this error from the backend\.

	•	Display a clear, non\-alarming message to the user: e\.g\., "You've reached your daily usage limit for AI features\. Please try again tomorrow\." or "Giani\.ai is experiencing high demand\. You can try this feature again in a few hours or tomorrow\." \(The second message is softer if you don't want to explicitly state individual limits initially\)\.

__	•	Preventing Further Submissions \(Temporarily\):__

	•	If a 429 is received, the frontend could temporarily disable AI generation buttons for a period or until the next day, showing a tooltip explaining the limit\.

__	•	Request Counting is Simpler for MVP:__ Easier to implement and understand\. You can set a limit like "50 AI generations per day\."
